newsitem.title: GUYANA: Guyana leader still in serious condition in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Guyana leader still in serious condition in U.S.

text.p: Guyana's President Cheddi Jagan shows signs of improvement after surgery in the United States to clear a blocked artery but is still in serious condition, government officials said on Thursday.
Guyana's state-run Information Service said the 78-year-old leader showed less dependency on drugs to support his blood pressure and "continuing improvement of his respiratory system."
But tests at Walter Reed Army Medical Centre near Washington have indicated "the need for continued life support systems."
Doctors performed a procedure called angioplasty on Jagan to clear blocked arteries after he was flown to Washington on Saturday complaining of heart pains.
His son Cheddi Jagan Jr. said his father was "alert and communicating in his own way," a reference to the fact he could not speak and was writing notes with a felt pen.
"There is still a little road to go and we'll have a more definitive picture in a couple of days," he told Reuters by telephone from the hospital on Wednesday night.
He said President Bill Clinton called Jagan's American-born wife Janet to express hope for a speedy recovery.

There was no indication how long Jagan would remain in the hospital. His doctor said on Saturday before he was flown to the United States that surgery meant the president could be away for two to three months.
Jagan led his left-leaning People's Progressive Party to victory at the polls in October 1992 -- Guyana's first democratic elections in 28 years. He has said he intends to seek re-election this year.
